claim: The mechanism behind the sub-FLOPs wall-clock penalty is that attention runs at much higher MFU than the rest of the training step: a two-component fit to the measured 500M A100 curve puts attention at ~73% of peak and the non-attention remainder at ~21%, so raising attention's share from 36% at 4k to 82% at 32k lifts blended MFU from 39.9% to 63.9%.
stance_target: the corpus critic's hypothesis that the 4k baseline is launch/overhead-bound at ~40% MFU while the 32k run amortizes better
scope_conditions: derived by solving a two-component MFU model against the measured 500M A100 points; attention share computed from the dataset's own achieved_tflops and tokens_per_second
